overall_conclusion: Across 2 waves and 15+ image models (static multi-layer USFM, ResNet50-ImageNet, 9 temporal architectures, cross-modal fusion, lag-bridge), image-based DL does NOT recover the GBTM biometry-trajectory phenotypes above the size-only ceiling. The recovery is a clean, controls-backed, encoder- AND architecture-general NULL. Where GBTM on biometry finds cohesive phenotypes (ARI 0.86, deceleration-driven), images are blind to them: the cohesive structure lives in the biometry growth-curve shape, and ultrasound appearance (an eco-visit-dominated maturation/plane/site clock near-orthogonal to growth) carries no non-redundant channel to it. The image maturation-lag is a real representational marker but recovers FGR only as a size proxy. This is a well-powered biological finding, not a modeling failure.

region_sweep.FINAL_VERDICT: All 6 model families agree: introducing images into the trajectory/GBTM framework produces NO NEW DISTINCTIVE REGIONS. Tested: joint biometry+image trajectory VAE, trajectory-coeff+image-lag fusion clustering, stacked image-PCA channel, single-component PCA sweep (PC1-8), cumulative image-dimensionality sweep (dim1-8), and gold-standard multivariate multlcmm biometry-only vs +image-lag. Every image variant is within its image-shuffle null (multlcmm ARI=1.000 identical to shuffled). The multivariate biometry GBMTM is a valid stronger baseline but adds no new regions over univariate EFW GBTM (faltering is symmetric, no head-sparing split); the multivariate coefficient space is a continuum, and the univariate EFW GBTM (3 cohesive trajectory phenotypes, subsample ARI 0.86-0.88) remains the most distinctive analyzable region model. Images are a maturation axis orthogonal to the growth-trajectory regions and to all clinical tabular data. Canonical config-B UNCHANGED.
